findings.title: Lightness values transposed for .topic-meta-data h5 a
findings.body: Inside `.topic-meta-data h5 a` the original CSS was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%);` (a darker shade used for bold meta text). The patch changed it to `color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%));`. Because `dark-light-choose(A, B)` returns `A` in the light theme, the rendered color in the default (light) theme is now `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)` instead of the original 30%, making this bold link much lighter than intended in light mode. The light branch should still be `$primary` at 30%, e.g. `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`.

findings.title: .group-member-info .name color regressed in light theme
findings.body: Inside `.group-member-info .name` the original CSS was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%);` (a dimmer shade of primary text). The patch changed it to `color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%));`. Since `dark-light-choose` evaluates to its first argument in the light theme, the rendered color is now `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)` rather than 30%, visibly lightening group-member names on user pages in the default theme. Should be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))` to preserve the original light-theme color.

findings.title: .custom-message-length color regressed in light theme
findings.body: Inside `.custom-message-length` the original CSS was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%);` (a lighter, less prominent helper text in modals). The patch changed it to `color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%));`. Because `dark-light-choose(A, B)` returns `A` in the light theme, the rendered color is now `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` instead of the original 70%, making the “characters remaining” helper much darker / more prominent than intended on mobile. Should be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))` to preserve the original light-theme color.

findings.title: .topic-map h3 color regressed in light theme
findings.body: Inside `.topic-map h3` the original CSS was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%);` (a very dark, prominent heading). The patch changed it to `color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%));`. Since `dark-light-choose(A, B)` returns `A` in the light theme, the rendered color is now `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)` instead of the original 20%, dramatically lightening the topic-map headings on mobile. Should be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 80%))` to preserve the original light-theme color.

findings.title: .group-member-info .name color regressed in light theme
findings.body: Inside `.group-member-info .name` the original CSS was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%);` (a darker shade for muted group member text). The patch changed it to `color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%));`. Since `dark-light-choose` resolves to its first argument in the light theme, the rendered color is now `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)` instead of the original 30%, lightening group-member names on the mobile user page in the default theme. Should be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))` to preserve the original light-theme color.
